Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-prompt-medium-0130", "row_sha256": "cfa2d4f51871f9581651f99d3f20f61378746cb2aa42fc9e41ffb38d728c9685", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "hey can you put together an update on the shared studio access list for the week of may 12. we have 14 people on it right now. sam was added may 14 as a day user through june 30. priya asked to have her access paused may 16 because she'll be away through may 28, but don't take her off the list. there are 11 working fobs, and two people need their fobs renewed. jo is still on there even though jo used to be a member; leave that entry alone for now because the coordinator hasn't checked if the storage locker is cleared yet. please make it a self-contained ordinary update, not a policy or a big explanation, and include those dates and details. the last part should assess where things stand, not add a general wrap-up: the list can be used for scheduled sessions, but it isn't a verified roster until jo's entry has been checked and the two fobs have been tested. if either test fails, say there's an access issue; we don't know yet whether either one will fail. keep the assessment to the list and these checks, don't make a conclusion about anyone's membership.", "output": "Draft a self-contained, ordinary update about the shared studio access list for the week of May 12. Include that 14 people are currently listed; Sam was added on May 14 as a day user through June 30; and Priya asked to have her access paused on May 16 while she is away through May 28. Keep Priya on the list. Note that 11 fobs are working and two people need fob renewals. Jo remains listed despite formerly being a member; leave Jo's entry unchanged for now because the coordinator has not yet checked whether the storage locker is cleared. Include these dates and details, and do not turn the update into a policy or an extended explanation.\n\nEnd with an assessment of the current list, not a general wrap-up: it can be used for scheduled sessions, but it is not a verified roster until Jo's entry has been checked and the two fobs have been tested. It is not yet known whether either fob test will fail; if either does fail, state that there is an access issue. Keep this assessment limited to the list and these checks, and do not draw conclusions about anyone's membership."}]
